component.name: MASCHERA
component.summary: Mask personal data in documents, entirely offline

description.p: MASCHERA finds and replaces personal data in documents — names, addresses, dates of birth, social security and case numbers — so a text can be shown, shared or given to an online service without handing over the people in it.

Everything happens on the machine. The document is not uploaded, and there is no endpoint that could send it anywhere. The model runs locally; the only time MASCHERA uses the network is the one download of that model on first start, and it asks before doing so.
Built for Swiss documents, in the three official languages of the Confederation — German, French and Italian — as well as English. Rumantsch is not supported.

This is pseudonymisation, not anonymisation: the replacements are kept in a dictionary, so a masked text can be turned back. That is a feature for reviewing a case, and a responsibility for storing the dictionary.

Fixes found while testing on macOS: the button that copies the prompt and opens the AI service now works there, and the app has its own icon. The environment variable MASCHERA_PORT works as documented, and error details from libraries no longer appear in responses of the local API.

Security update: raised minimum versions of the dependencies (torch, transformers, Flask, Werkzeug, Jinja2, gunicorn), the model is loaded from safetensors only, and training artifacts are no longer shipped. Model and detection are unchanged.
First public release: Linux (AppImage, Flatpak), Windows and Docker.
